nbis.headline: Fri US cash $221.07 (+0.62% / +$1.36 vs Thu $219.71); range $218.50–$225.11; AH $221.33 (+0.12%); vol ~9.5M vs ~20.2M avg; cap ~$60.1B. Still ~12% below Tue $249.87.

nbis.headline: No new issuer 6-K/8-K or holder filing since Goldman SC 13G/A 5.1% (0000886982-26-000526, 7 Oct). Next earnings Nov 10 per Yahoo.
nbis.why: Nothing new on dilution/funding over the weekend; price driver remains sector narrative.

nbis.headline: Weekend commentary frames the Thu −7.4% as a re-pricing of contract-backed neocloud debt after the FT OpenAI ARR (~$50B vs ~$68B whisper) report; cites $20–25B 2026 capex vs $3.0–3.4B revenue guide and $8.55B borrowings at end-June.
nbis.why: Thesis risk is funding cost / collateral confidence, not contracts. Next secured raise terms are the tell. Opinion piece, not a filing.

nbis.headline: Carry: Rosenblatt Buy PT $304 (initiated 8 Oct); Yahoo 1y target est $283.60.
nbis.why: Sell-side support unchanged; ~28% upside to Rosenblatt from Fri close.

aiInfra.headline: AMZN +3.29% Fri to $262.43: AWS CEO Garman says AI spend is not a bubble (production workloads); BNP sees AWS growth 43–45%; Amazon issued 10/30/100-year bonds to fund AI build.
aiInfra.why: Hyperscaler demand read-through positive for neoclouds/GPUs, but 100-year paper shows capex is now debt-funded.

aiInfra.headline: WSJ (via DataCenter Digest, Oct 11): SpaceX arranging ~$40B ($10B bank loans + $30B IG debt, Apollo lead) to buy Nvidia hardware; Broadcom seeking >$50B for OpenAI custom chips; Oracle in talks with Apollo/Goldman.
aiInfra.why: SPCX: more leverage on a balance sheet already ~$40B debt. NVDA: confirms large forward GPU orders. Sector: compute is increasingly debt-financed, same theme hitting NBIS.

macro.headline: US 10Y ~5.24% Fri close (Yahoo ^TNX), off Thu ~5.31%. US bond market closed Mon (Columbus Day); equities open.

macro.headline: Sept CPI Wed 14 Oct: consensus 3.7% y/y headline, 2.5% core (Reuters poll); PPI + retail sales Thu. Fed hiked in Sept; Oct 27–28 FOMC hike odds reduced but a hot print could revive them.
macro.why: Biggest event risk for the book this week.

macro.headline: Oil up on renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's main airport over the weekend; KOSPI opened −1.3% on inflation/Mideast worry.
macro.why: Energy-driven inflation pressure feeds the rate-hike risk and hits Asia semis first.

macro.headline: Bank earnings start Tue (JPM, GS, C, WFC); BAC, MS Wed.
macro.why: Credit commentary matters given how much AI capex is now debt/private-credit funded.

soWhat: NBIS stabilised Fri (+0.6%) on thin volume; no new filing, no FLAG.
Theme of the week: AI capex is debt-funded (AMZN 100y bonds, SpaceX $40B GPU loan) — funding cost is the NBIS risk.
SK Hynix −4.3% live in Korea's catch-up session; watch the close vs 5%.
CPI Wed + TSMC Thu decide direction; F&G 45 Fear, improving from 38.
